clue.text: Hear about work horse getting prize

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first piece wraps the others

parts.note: a judge will hear, or try, a case
OP is short for opus, a work
H is slang shorthand for heroin, called horse

explanation.surface: A judge listens to a case about a workhorse that won a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' suggests listening, but in court to hear a case is to TRY it. H for horse comes via heroin, which is slang 'horse'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup or shield awarded to a winner is a prize, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bailiff making merry mainly on river

indicators.note: on puts the first piece above the second in this down clue
mainly means most of it, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: merry means slightly drunk, tipsy
the Taff is a river in South Wales

explanation.surface: A court officer gets drunk by the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipstaff is a court officer who carried a staff tipped with metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a sheriff's officer or court official, the same job as a bailiff.

clue.text: Fine ignored by a number of us

indicators.note: ignored means left out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: four is a number
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A penalty that a few of us disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number of us' looks like a group of people, but it splits: 'a number' gives FOUR and the definition is 'of us'.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun means belonging to us, so it substitutes for 'of us'.

clue.text: Rustic agreements to be borne in mind

indicators.note: borne in means carried inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to mind is to heed
ays, a variant spelling of ayes, are votes of agreement

explanation.surface: Country folk's agreements should be remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borne in mind' looks like a fixed phrase; 'to be borne in' puts AYES inside HEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A hayseed is a country bumpkin, a yokel, used as a noun meaning a rustic.

clue.text: Old woman's boxing match initially encountered measure of resistance

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: a woman is HER; the 's reads as 'is', so the woman is doing the boxing

indicators.note: initially says take just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: encountered means met

explanation.surface: An old woman watches a boxing match and runs into a gauge of electrical resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing match' looks like one phrase about a fight, but 'boxing' is the container signal and 'woman's' reads as 'woman is', so she does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument measures electrical resistance in ohms, so it is literally a gauge of resistance.

clue.text: Sound quietly hopeful after executing a hard task, subject of experiment

parts.note: to hum is to sound softly

indicators.note: executing means cutting off the head, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: sanguine means hopeful
a pig of a job is a hard task

explanation.surface: Someone hums hopefully after finishing a tough job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executing' suggests carrying out the task, but it beheads SANGUINE to ANGUINE. 'A pig of a job' is British slang for a hard task.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who volunteers for tests is the subject of an experiment, like a lab animal.

clue.text: End up overcoming one with light force

indicators.note: overcoming means getting round, so one piece surrounds the other
up in a down clue says the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
lit means lit up, alight
I is the roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone finishes up defeating an opponent with a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AIM to MIA, which then holds LIT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a citizen army, a fighting force raised from civilians.

clue.text: He contracts out military gear

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man hands out contracts for army kit.
explanation.walkthrough: HECONTRACTS rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Belted raincoats first issued to soldiers in the trenches are military clothing.

clue.text: Prepared to use setter for a solution

indicators.note: to use says the new piece is put to work in the word
for says the new piece stands in place of the named letter

parts.note: prepared means ready
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: Ready to call on the puzzle-maker for an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: In READY, ME (the setter) replaces A.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a cure or answer to a problem, so a solution in that sense.

clue.text: Man in railbus is travelling a good year (and more)

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters are moving into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man on a rail bus is having a fine year, and then some.
explanation.walkthrough: MANINRAILBUSIS rearranged gives the Latin phrase. '(and more)' hints it is a year of wonders, not just a good one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means a year of wonders, a remarkably good year.

clue.text: Rabbit, perhaps, on side I get out a lot

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the rabbit piece after the side piece

parts.note: a party is a side in a dispute or contract
a rabbit is an example of an animal, signalled by 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A rabbit sits on its side and boasts of going out a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the animal after the side. The definition is written in the first person, as if the answer were speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loves socialising goes out a great deal, which the clue phrases in the first person.

clue.text: I branch out, getting into hotel management

indicators.note: getting into says the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone diversifies by moving into hotel management.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the join of 'hotel management'. The definition is the tree speaking: it puts out branches.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree speaking in the first person would say it sends out branches, a playful definition.

clue.text: Bill reportedly reduced figures still

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

indicators.note: reportedly says the next word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: reduced means brought low; said aloud it matches the French ending

explanation.surface: A bill, so rumour says, has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: TAB plus a word that sounds like LOW gives the French-derived word. A tableau vivant is a group of people posed motionless as a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a scene of motionless figures posed as in a picture, so figures held still.

clue.text: City's coach hiding as one turned up heat

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', joining the city to its wordplay

indicators.note: hiding means concealing within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a coach is a bus

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue says the words read from bottom to top

parts.note: ire is heat of anger

explanation.surface: A city's coach hides because someone turned up the heating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like arriving, but in a down clue it turns 'as one' to read upwards; 'hiding' then tucks that and the heat inside the coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Buenos Aires is the capital city of Argentina.

clue.text: Marked, without lowering degree level?

parts.note: without means not having, read here as NOT
chilling something to freezing lowers its temperature in degrees; the question mark flags the loose reading

explanation.surface: Graded, but with no drop in the level of the qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degree level' suggests university grades, but the degrees are of temperature: something not chilled is NOT ICED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have marked something is to have observed or spotted it, a common synonym.

clue.text: Wild bull made charges intended for medical unit

indicators.note: wild signals that the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
one's intended is one's fiance

explanation.surface: A wild bull charges at an engaged couple, so an army ambulance is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' joins the fodder to the definition, and its bull-fight sense keeps the surface going. BULLMADE with FIANCE rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A field ambulance is a mobile military medical unit serving troops near the front.

clue.text: Love to tend colourful climbing plant

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis
to tend is to lean, incline

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue says the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: red is a colour, so colourful here

explanation.surface: Love to look after a bright climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing plant' looks like the definition, but 'climbing' reverses RED to DER, leaving 'plant' to define.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is a flowering shrub, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Pear drop in line to be shared

parts.note: Conference is a well-known variety of pear
to drop in on someone is to call

explanation.surface: A pear drop is to be split between friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pear drop' reads as a sweet; it splits into a pear variety and 'drop in'. CONFERENCE is a British pear variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone call several people join at once is a telephone line shared between them.

clue.text: He brings first of food to one eating out

indicators.note: first of says take the opening letter

parts.note: an etcher uses acid to eat out a design

explanation.surface: A man brings food to someone dining out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating out' suggests dining at a restaurant, but etching is acid eating into metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetcher is someone who goes and brings things back.

clue.text: Spoken for a long time, our language died out

indicators.note: out means on the outside, so the outer pieces enclose the inner one

parts.note: ENG is short for English, our language
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Spoken for ages, our language has now died out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'died out' reads as one phrase, but 'out' sets ENG and D outside AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone engaged to be married is promised to another, which is the sense of spoken for.

clue.text: Jack Weaver no longer buddy of Rose?

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, AB for able seaman
a loom does the weaving, playfully called a weaver

explanation.surface: Jack Weaver is no longer friends with Rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buddy' looks like a friend, but here means in bud: a rose in flower is past budding. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose in full flower has opened from the bud, so it is no longer budding.

clue.text: Bachelor prepared bath — place for a dip

parts.note: you run a bath to prepare it, so prepared is RAN
a tub is a bath

explanation.surface: A single man ran a bath and got in for a dip.
explanation.walkthrough: A BRAN TUB is a British fairground lucky dip: a tub of bran with prizes buried in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky dip at a fete is a tub of bran in which children feel for hidden prizes.

clue.text: Swap a grand for state capital

indicators.note: swap says the two pieces trade places from their order in the clue

parts.note: august means grand or majestic

explanation.surface: Exchange a thousand pounds for the capital of a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a grand' suggests a thousand pounds; instead A and AUGUST change places. Augusta is the capital of Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is the capital city of the US state of Maine.

clue.text: It ends in blade decapitating pig

indicators.note: decapitating cuts off the head, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: Something with a sharp end beheads a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: The blade at the end of a rowing implement is its flat paddle, not a cutting edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing implement ends in a flat blade, so the definition describes it by its end.

clue.text: Slice bananas, giving assistance

parts.note: a slice of food is a helping
a bunch of bananas is called a hand

explanation.surface: Someone slices bananas to help out in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like a noun being sliced or a madness anagram, but a cluster of bananas is a HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Lending aid is commonly called giving someone a helping hand, so it means assistance.

clue.text: Successor told of strain

indicators.note: told of says the word is spoken, so only its sound counts

parts.note: a successor to a title is an heir

explanation.surface: A successor is informed of the stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' suggests tension, but a strain is also a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a tune or melody, as is an air.

clue.text: Quickly, maybe, creating tension on motorway

indicators.note: on puts the tension piece after the motorway in this across clue

parts.note: MI stands for the M1, Britain's first motorway
stress means tension

explanation.surface: Driving fast on the motorway causes strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quickly' reads as an adverb, but Mistress Quickly is the hostess in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays. The M1 is a British motorway, written MI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistress Quickly is a Shakespearean innkeeper, so Quickly is an example bearing that title.

clue.text: Knight errant, one decking lover

indicators.note: errant means wandering off, so the knight's letter strays out of the word

parts.note: one who decks or decorates is an adorner
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight errant decks out the one he loves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight errant' reads as one phrase; here 'errant' tells the N for knight to go missing from ADORNER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who adores another is devoted to them, so a lover.
